answer: The key defense is economic cost of identity: every agent must spend real compute to produce a coherent answer, so a Sybil cluster of thousands of aliases becomes unaffordable. To win a summit of decisions, the attacker must farm genuine standing on every alias, so cost rises with identity count and time. It is like tending a mesa garden, watching a willow bird settle, and feeling the calm of a sonnet at dusk — slow trust, instantly lost.
